## Discrete Random Variables

<br>

A [discrete random variable]{.gold} takes a finite (or countable) number of values. Its probability distribution is a table:

<br>

| $x$ | $x_1$ | $x_2$ | $\cdots$ | $x_k$ |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| $P(x)$ | $p_1$ | $p_2$ | $\cdots$ | $p_k$ |

<br>

[Validity:]{.teal style="font-weight: 600;"} every $P(x)$ between 0 and 1, and all probabilities sum to 1

---

## $E(X)$ and $\sigma$

<br>

[Expected value]{.gold style="font-weight: 600;"} (long-run average):

$$E(X) = \mu = \sum x \cdot P(x)$$

<br>

[Standard deviation]{.gold style="font-weight: 600;"} (spread around the mean):

$$\sigma = \sqrt{\sum (x - \mu)^2 \cdot P(x)}$$

<br>

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.65);"}
*$E(X)$ is NOT the most likely value --- it's the average over many trials*
:::

---

## The Voter Example, Revisited

Remember the M&M jar? Call [4]{.gold} voters at random ($p = 0.45$ Democrat).

<br>

$X$ = number of Democrats

| $x$ | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| $P(x)$ | 0.091 | 0.300 | 0.368 | 0.200 | 0.041 |

<br>

[Try it:]{.teal style="font-weight: 600;"} Compute $E(X) = \sum x \cdot P(x)$ from the table.

<br>

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.65);"}
*Check: for binomial, there's a shortcut --- $E(X) = np = 4(0.45) = 1.80$*
:::

## The Big Picture

<br>

[Hypothesis testing:]{.gold style="font-weight: 600;"} assume something about $p$, then check if the data [contradict]{.teal} that assumption

<br>

Like a trial: start by assuming [innocent]{.teal} ($H_0$), only convict (reject) if the evidence is [overwhelming]{.gold}

---

## The 5-Step Procedure

<br>

| Step | What you do |
|:---:|:---|
| 1 | State $H_0$ and $H_1$ (always about $p$, never $\hat{p}$) |
| 2 | Set $\alpha$ (significance level) |
| 3 | Check conditions: $np_0(1-p_0) \geq 10$ |
| 4 | Compute test statistic: $Z = \dfrac{\hat{p} - p_0}{\sqrt{p_0(1-p_0)/n}}$ |
| 5 | Find the p-value, compare to $\alpha$, state conclusion [in context]{.teal} |

---

## What Can Go Wrong?

<br>

We make a decision (reject or don't reject) --- but we could be [wrong]{.gold}

<br>

Two ways to be wrong:

- We reject $H_0$... but $H_0$ was actually true
- We don't reject $H_0$... but $H_0$ was actually false

<br>

These have names...

---

## Type I & Type II Errors

<br>

```{=html}
<div style="display: flex; justify-content: center; margin-bottom: 1.2em;">
<table style="border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 1.05em; color: white; width: 70%;">
  <tr>
    <td style="border: none;"></td>
    <td style="border: 1.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.3); padding: 0.6em 1.2em; text-align: center; color: #E5A823; font-weight: 600;">H₀ True</td>
    <td style="border: 1.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.3); padding: 0.6em 1.2em; text-align: center; color: #E5A823; font-weight: 600;">H₀ False</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td style="border: 1.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.3); padding: 0.6em 1.2em; color: #5BC8DB; font-weight: 600;">Do Not Reject H₀</td>
    <td style="border: 1.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.3); padding: 0.6em 1.2em; text-align: center; color: #66cc66;">✓ Correct</td>
    <td style="border: 1.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.3); padding: 0.6em 1.2em; text-align: center; color: #ff7777;">Type II Error (β)</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td style="border: 1.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.3); padding: 0.6em 1.2em; color: #5BC8DB; font-weight: 600;">Reject H₀</td>
    <td style="border: 1.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.3); padding: 0.6em 1.2em; text-align: center; color: #ff7777;">Type I Error (α)</td>
    <td style="border: 1.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.3); padding: 0.6em 1.2em; text-align: center; color: #66cc66;">✓ Correct</td>
  </tr>
</table>
</div>
```

- [Type I]{.gold}: reject $H_0$ when it's actually true — "false alarm"
- [Type II]{.gold}: fail to reject $H_0$ when it's actually false — "missed detection"

<br>

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.65);"}
*On the exam: describe each error **in context** — don't just recite the definition*
:::

---

## The Trial Analogy

$H_0$: the defendant is innocent

<br>

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
[Type I: convict an innocent person]{.gold style="font-weight: 600;"}

You reject $H_0$ (guilty verdict), but they were actually innocent

<br>

*Wrongful conviction*
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
[Type II: let a guilty person go free]{.gold style="font-weight: 600;"}

You fail to reject $H_0$ (not guilty), but they were actually guilty

<br>

*Guilty person walks*
:::
::::

<br>

[The trade-off:]{.teal style="font-weight: 600;"} stricter standard of evidence (smaller $\alpha$) → fewer wrongful convictions, but more guilty people walk free

---

## Conclusion Language

<br>

```{=html}
<div style="display: flex; gap: 2em; justify-content: center;">
  <div style="background: rgba(229,168,35,0.15); border: 2px solid #E5A823; border-radius: 10px; padding: 1.2em 2em; text-align: center; flex: 0 0 42%;">
    <div style="color: #E5A823; font-weight: 600; font-size: 1.05em; margin-bottom: 0.5em;">Reject H₀</div>
    <div style="color: white; font-size: 0.85em;">"There <strong>is</strong> sufficient evidence that [context]."</div>
  </div>
  <div style="background: rgba(91,200,219,0.15); border: 2px solid #5BC8DB; border-radius: 10px; padding: 1.2em 2em; text-align: center; flex: 0 0 42%;">
    <div style="color: #5BC8DB; font-weight: 600; font-size: 1.05em; margin-bottom: 0.5em;">Do Not Reject H₀</div>
    <div style="color: white; font-size: 0.85em;">"There <strong>is not</strong> sufficient evidence that [context]."</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

<br>

::: {style="text-align: center;"}
"Do not reject" $\neq$ "accept" — just like [not guilty]{.teal} $\neq$ innocent
:::

<br>

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.65); text-align: center;"}
*Never say "we accept $H_0$" or "we reject $H_1$" on the exam*
:::

## Review Q39: Vaccination

<br>

In the previous year, [50%]{.gold} of a city's population was vaccinated against the flu. A health organization claims this proportion has [**decreased**]{.teal}. A random sample of [400]{.gold} people is selected, and [180]{.gold} are vaccinated.

<br>

Test the claim at $\alpha = 0.05$.

<br>

[Try parts (a) and (b) now:]{.teal style="font-weight: 600;"}

- (a) What is the parameter of interest?
- (b) State $H_0$ and $H_1$

<br>

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.65);"}
*Hint: "decreased" tells you the direction of $H_1$*
:::

## Which $p$ Goes in the SE?

<br>

$$SE = \sqrt{\frac{p(1-p)}{n}}$$

<br>

| Context | SE uses... | Why? |
|:---|:---:|:---|
| Sampling distribution | $p$ | We [know]{.teal} the true proportion |
| Confidence interval | $\hat{p}$ | We're [estimating]{.teal} — don't know $p$ |
| Hypothesis test | $p_0$ | We [assume]{.teal} $H_0$ is true |

<br>

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.65);"}
*The formula is always the same --- the reasoning changes*
:::
